title: Degree-zero Cech column augmentation identifies homology
statement: Let X be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], U an arbitrary family of opens, F an O_X-module [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], and I an injective resolution [def-sp-injective-resolutions]. Let D = moduleCechDouble U I and A be the Cech complex of F [def-sc-module-cech-comparison]. The image a of the resolution augmentation is a morphism A → D.X 0. For any proof ha that a ≫ D.d 0 1 = 0 and any Cech degree n, the map from A.X n concentrated in degree zero to D.flip.X n induced by a.f n is a quasi-isomorphism in degree ZERO. No positive-cohomology vanishing hypothesis is needed.

source.place: Beta augmentation and its zeroth column homology, expanded by left exactness in Tag 01DZ

proof.text: The augmentation F → I^0 is the kernel of I^0 → I^1 by [def-sp-injective-resolutions]. Evaluate on each tuple intersection: sections preserve kernels, so the evaluated augmentation remains a kernel. Restriction of scalars does not change the underlying kernel.

The column of [def-sc-module-cech-comparison] is the product over tuples. Kernels commute with products coordinatewise, so the augmentation identifies Cech n-cochains with the column kernel. Degree zero has no incoming boundaries, and the source is concentrated in degree zero. Thus the induced degree-zero homology map is invertible. Empty tuple-index products and empty opens give zero modules, and the identification still holds.

lean.statement: theorem moduleCech_resolution_column_zero {X : Scheme.{u}} {ι : Type u} (U : ι → X.Opens) (F : X.Modules) (I : InjectiveResolution F) (ha : (CategoryTheory.cechComplexFunctor U).map ((PresheafOfModules.forgetToPresheafModuleCat (op ⊤) isTerminalTop.op).map (I.ι.f 0).val) ≫ (moduleCechDouble U I).d 0 1 = 0) (n : ℕ) : let A := (CategoryTheory.cechComplexFunctor U).obj F.presheafModuleCat let a : A ⟶ (moduleCechDouble U I).X 0 := (CategoryTheory.cechComplexFunctor U).map ((PresheafOfModules.forgetToPresheafModuleCat (op ⊤) isTerminalTop.op).map (I.ι.f 0).val) QuasiIsoAt ((CochainComplex.fromSingle₀Equiv ((moduleCechDouble U I).flip.X n) (A.X n)).symm ⟨a.f n, by simpa [a, A, moduleCechDouble] using congrArg (fun f ↦ f.f n) ha⟩) 0
